- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.67) and forecast is flat or rising slowly, model underestimates peak prices — correct by adding 2–5% to forecast for early bullish momentum.
- After a sharp spike (e.g., >10% from prior day), model often overcorrects downward — reduce forecast slope by 10–20% for next 5–7 days to avoid overshoot.
- If official event net is negative (supply net <0) and sentiment is mixed or bearish, model tends to overpredict decline — adjust downward by 3–8% if sentiment <0.33.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30d horizon when sentiment is volatile — if forecast is >10% above recent 7d average, reduce by 1–3% per day until convergence.
- In high-event periods (≥20 events/30d), model often fails to capture event-driven volatility — add 1–3% to forecast if sentiment is bullish and event count >15.
- If sentiment is bearish and forecast is rising, model is overconfident — reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 3–5 days unless event context is strongly bullish.
